recipes.name: Mile-High Apple Pie
ingredients_raw: 8 large Golden Delicious apples - peeled, cored and cut into 1/8 inch slices
0.25 cup cold unsalted butter, cut into 1/4-inch pieces
1 recipe pastry for a 10-inch double crust pie

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C). Position an oven rack in the lower part of the oven; place a baking stone on it.
Toss apples with lemon juice in a large bowl; set aside.
Stir ¾ cup sugar, potato starch, cinnamon, and nutmeg together in a separate bowl; set aside.

Divide pastry dough in half. Roll 1 dough half out on a lightly floured surface to fit a 10-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate. Pile ½ apples into crust, dot with ½ butter pieces, and sprinkle with ½ potato starch mixture. Pile remaining ½ apples on top, dot with remaining ½ butter pieces, and sprinkle with remaining ½ potato starch mixture. Roll out remaining 1 dough half; carefully place over apples. Pinch and crimp edges to seal crusts. Poke a few holes in top crust using a fork. Brush top crust with milk; sprinkle with remaining 1 tablespoon sugar.

Place on the baking stone in the preheated oven; immediately reduce the oven temperature to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Bake until crust is golden brown, about 1 hour checking halfway through baking time, covering edges with aluminum foil if needed to prevent over-browning during the last 30 minutes. Cool on a wire rack before serving, 3 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Mile-High Apple Pie
raw_recipe.description: This mile-high apple pie recipe stands tall. Potato starch, sugar, cinnamon, and freshly grated nutmeg season the apples and keeps their juices stable.

review.reviewBody: Wow wow and double wow!! I can't believe how AWESOME this recipe is! I took it to a church potluck and there wasn't a crumb left and got many requests for the recipe. It is really juicy but not runny at all. Next time I think I will bump up the cinnaman since we love extra spice but most will probably find the original amount just fine. You HAVE to try this!

Perfect apple pie recipe! I've made this pie 3 times and every time it's a hit. Tastes much better than store bought. Like others, I used corn starch instead of potato starch and it works just fine. I always use a crust recipe from the book, The Secrets of Baking. These two recipes combined makes the perfect pie!

I've made this pie twice and it's now the ONLY apple pie that my family wants! I used fresh Cortland apples, part brown sugar, cornstarch instead of potato, and cheated by using pre-made crust and it came out fabulous. Even better than my mother-in-law's ... and that's saying a lot!

FANTASTIC Pie recipe! I used two granny smith, two golden delicious and 2 Fuji apples to give the pie a little more taste and texture and I was pleased with the way it came out. Used corn starch as that's what I had on hand and it didn't seem to make any difference, still came out nice and juicy, yet not soupy. I also added walnuts in with the sugar mixture and the husband loved it.

I used 5 granny smith and 3 golden delicious apples and subbed arrowroot starch since I didn't have any potato starch. Put it in a Pillsbury gluten free pie crust, and hubby told me it was the best pie he's had since going gluten free several years ago! I'll definitely make this again!

This pie is delicious!! I did make a few substitutions though. In place of 3/4 cup white sugar, I used 1/2c white sugar and 1/4 brown sugar. I also increased the cinnamon to closer to 2tsp as we enjoy our pie with more spice. Also increased the nutmeg a wee bit. I didn’t have potato starch so used corn starch instead and it worked out just fine. The pie is not soupy when cut into, but also not dry. I will definitely make this one again!

I made this last year for the first time at Thanksgiving. Everyone loved it and was really surprised how well a "non" cook or baker for that matter could make an apple pie that was just perfect in every way. The only thing that I changed was I added carmel sauce on top of the apples before I covered them with the 2nd crust. Absolutely wonderful!
great recipe, I did parcook the apples before placing them in the crust so I didnt get settling and that also made it work better.

The taste was awesome, and I loved how the juices didn't flow all over the place when the pie was cut. I will note that I used cornstarch in lieu of potato starch...and I also used 1 1/2 teaspoons apple cider vinegar for the lemon juice. (I didn't want to go to the store for the ingredients I didn't have) One major change I will make for next time is just blending the sugar mixture in with the apples before putting the apples in the crust. After it finished baking, there was stll a heavy layer of t atop the apples...otherwise still very delicious...and nice and gooey.
Delicious! I use a mix of baking apples rather than all golden delicious and since I never have potato starch on hand, I just use corn starch. This is the pie people ask for at every holiday!

This is great! Used granny smith's, as they were on hand. Also used 1/2 cup regular and 1/2 cup brown sugar. Did not have a baking stone, so just put foil under pie pan - but no leakage anyway. Wonderful apple flavor!

I gave this recipe a try. After the first bite, my family and friends asked me, what happened? I don't know if it was the different apple, potato starch, or lack of spices that I usually use, but everyone pushed it away after the first bite.

I made it for the first time for Christmas lunch. Prayed everyone would like it, considering I had never cooked for them.They argued about how to split it up to take home with them, so a definite hit.
Can I use crescent rollout pastry for the apple pie crust and apple crisp apples
This was a great recipe! It was balanced and not overly sweet. The potato starch was so much better than the flour I typically use.
Too liquidy but the flavor was good.
I used a crumble topping instead of a top crust. It turned out great!
This was a decent recipe, but I felt it needed to be a little sweeter, and a little less apples. I will make again!
Love, love, love this pie!

This pie challenged my apple stacking skills, but it was so worth it. There is just enough sugar and spice to make any true sweet eater happy mixed with a generous amount of apples for the true apple pie fan. In this house you get two sticky thumbs up.
